name: fix_java_insecure_deserialization
description: Fixes Java native deserialization RCE: ObjectInputStream.readObject() on untrusted bytes instantiates arbitrary classes
prompts: SessionStore.deserialize(byte[] data) in src/main/java/com/optarena/app/SessionStore.java restores a session payload back into a Map<String,Object>. It calls ObjectInputStream.readObject() directly on the untrusted bytes - Java native deserialization instantiates whatever class the stream names and runs its readObject() method, a well-known remote-code-execution vector. The session format is being migrated to JSON: legitimate payloads are now produced with Jackson (com.fasterxml.jackson.databind.ObjectMapper, already a dependency). Rewrite deserialize to parse the bytes as JSON via ObjectMapper and return the resulting Map<String,Object>, so an untrusted payload can never instantiate an arbitrary Java object. Do NOT keep any ObjectInputStream fallback for "legacy" sessions - that would still be exploitable. Keep the class name and the deserialize(byte[]) signature.
